profile.subject: Leonardo da Vinci
profile.overview: Leonardo da Vinci was an Italian Renaissance painter and engineer who worked in Florence and Milan and spent his last years in France. He painted the **Mona Lisa** and **The Last Supper**, and filled notebooks with studies of subjects as different as the valves of the heart and the flight of birds.

key_moments.title: An angel in Verrocchio’s workshop
key_moments.text: Leonardo trained in the Florence workshop of **Andrea del Verrocchio**. Both artists worked on *The Baptism of Christ*, a panel with two angels kneeling by the river. The Uffizi credits Leonardo with the angel on the left and suggests that his hand may also be visible in the river landscape behind it.
claims: Leonardo da Vinci trained in Andrea del Verrocchio’s workshop in Florence.
Leonardo da Vinci and Andrea del Verrocchio both worked on The Baptism of Christ, dated to about 1470–1475.
The Uffizi attributes the angel on the left of The Baptism of Christ to Leonardo da Vinci and considers that Leonardo may also have painted the river landscape.

key_moments.title: The Last Supper in Milan
key_moments.text: For **Ludovico Sforza**, Leonardo painted the wall of a dining hall at Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan. The painted room seems to extend the real one. Working on dry plaster gave Leonardo time to revise the scene, but the same technique helped cause the paint to flake soon after he finished.
claims: Leonardo da Vinci painted The Last Supper around 1495–1498 for Ludovico Sforza in the dining hall of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan.
The perspective of The Last Supper makes the painted chamber seem to extend the dining hall.
Leonardo da Vinci painted The Last Supper on dry plaster to allow changes.
The dry technique contributed to pigment loss soon after The Last Supper was finished.

key_moments.title: Leonardo begins the Mona Lisa
key_moments.text: Leonardo portrayed **Lisa Gherardini**, the wife of a Florentine silk merchant, in the act of turning toward the viewer. He used glazes to soften the edges of her features. He kept the portrait for years, continuing to work on it.
claims: Leonardo da Vinci began the Mona Lisa around 1503.
The Mona Lisa depicts Lisa Gherardini, the wife of the Florentine silk merchant Francesco del Giocondo.
Leonardo da Vinci depicted Lisa Gherardini turning toward the viewer and used glazes to soften edges in the Mona Lisa.
Leonardo da Vinci kept the Mona Lisa for years and continued to work on it.

key_moments.title: A new patron in France
key_moments.text: **Francis I** invited Leonardo to France, where he settled at the Clos Lucé in Amboise and served the king as a painter, architect and engineer. Leonardo studied the region’s waterways and drew up plans for a royal palace and town at Romorantin.
claims: Francis I invited Leonardo da Vinci to France in 1516, and Leonardo da Vinci settled at the Clos Lucé in Amboise.
Leonardo da Vinci served Francis I as painter, architect and engineer.
Leonardo da Vinci studied local waterways and drew up plans for a royal palace and town at Romorantin.

deep_facts.text: While surveying strongholds for Cesare Borgia in 1502, Leonardo drew **a map of Imola** that set the town’s streets inside a circle. Around the rim he wrote the names of winds at the eight points of the compass.
claims: Leonardo da Vinci drew a plan of Imola in 1502 while surveying strongholds for Cesare Borgia.
Leonardo da Vinci drew Imola’s street plan inside a circle and wrote wind names at the eight compass points.

deep_facts.text: Leonardo studied the hearts of oxen and sketched a mould for a **glass model of the aortic valve**, the flap that controls blood leaving the heart for the body. In his notes, he linked the valve’s closing to eddies in the blood. The Royal Collection describes the glass model as something Leonardo made, though researchers who reconstructed the flow still question whether he built it.
claims: Leonardo da Vinci studied the heart valves of oxen and drew a mould for a glass model of the aortic valve.
Leonardo da Vinci linked eddies in the blood to the closing of the aortic valve.

The Royal Collection catalogue describes a glass model that Leonardo da Vinci built, while an experimental study by Morteza Gharib and colleagues questions whether Leonardo da Vinci actually built it.

deep_facts.text: Leonardo’s **Codex on the Flight of Birds** puts notes on birds and flying machines into his right-to-left mirror script. He assembled it from partly used sheets, some of them already marked with reddish sketches of plants.
claims: Leonardo da Vinci’s Codex on the Flight of Birds contains mirror writing and studies of bird flight and flying machines.
Leonardo da Vinci compiled the Codex on the Flight of Birds from partly used sheets that still show reddish sketches, including sketches of plants.

connections.name: Cesare Borgia

connections.name: Raphael
connections.connection: Drew on Leonardo’s Mona Lisa when composing his portraits of Agnolo and Maddalena Doni.

connections.name: Vitruvius

uncovered: deep_facts.1.text: The gloss calls the aortic valve a single flap and specifies that the outgoing blood travels to the body. The cited passage describes valve closure and flow but does not establish that structure or destination. Remove the gloss or use evidence that directly supports accurate anatomy.

deep_facts.1.text: The description of the researchers as having reconstructed the flow lacks a finding supported by the excerpt. The abstract reports laboratory flow imaging. Use that description or cite methods that establish exactly what was reconstructed.
issues: key_moments.1.date: The Cenacolo Vinciano table and Museo Leonardiano give 1495–1498, while the Cenacolo Vinciano narrative and conservation material allow a 1494 start. Explicitly acknowledge the variant or use a broader approximate date that covers it.

key_moments.1.text: The conservation excerpt supports early pigment loss and a contribution from the dry technique, but it does not specify flaking. Say the technique contributed to early paint loss or cite evidence for flaking.

key_moments.2.date: The Louvre places the beginning of the Mona Lisa around 1503, while the Museo Leonardiano chronology puts its beginning in a 1504–1506 entry. Attribute the circa 1503 date to the Louvre or use a broader early-1500s date.

key_moments.3.text: The Clos Lucé excerpt explicitly describes plans for an ideal town and says Leonardo conceived a royal palace. Direct evidence for drawn palace plans is missing. Say he envisioned a palace and drew up plans for a town at Romorantin, or cite evidence for both plans.

deep_facts.1.text: The only researchers cited asked in 2002 whether Leonardo built the model and reported evidence for that possibility. The word “still” presents that older open question as current. Date the study and say it left construction open, or provide current evidence.

connections.4.connection: The Accademia record confirms that Leonardo cites Vitruvius in the drawing notes, but cautions that the proportions follow Alberti and that Leonardo probably knew Vitruvius’s treatise only to a limited extent. Replace the unqualified causal claim with the documented citation in the notes to Vitruvian Man.

key_moments.1.text: The conservation excerpt supports early pigment loss and a contribution from the dry technique, but it does not specify flaking. Say the technique contributed to early paint loss or cite evidence for flaking.

key_moments.2.date: The Louvre places the beginning of the Mona Lisa around 1503, while the Museo Leonardiano chronology puts its beginning in a 1504–1506 entry. Attribute the circa 1503 date to the Louvre or use a broader early-1500s date.

key_moments.3.text: The Clos Lucé excerpt explicitly describes plans for an ideal town and says Leonardo conceived a royal palace. Direct evidence for drawn palace plans is missing. Say he envisioned a palace and drew up plans for a town at Romorantin, or cite evidence for both plans.

deep_facts.1.text: The only researchers cited asked in 2002 whether Leonardo built the model and reported evidence for that possibility. The word “still” presents that older open question as current. Date the study and say it left construction open, or provide current evidence.

connections.4.connection: The Accademia record confirms that Leonardo cites Vitruvius in the drawing notes, but cautions that the proportions follow Alberti and that Leonardo probably knew Vitruvius’s treatise only to a limited extent. Replace the unqualified causal claim with the documented citation in the notes to Vitruvian Man.
